bicep-first-words.title: What Bicep Does
bicep-first-words.code:
param greeting string = 'Hello, CloudSeam'
output message string = greeting
bicep-first-words.task: Change Hello, CloudSeam to Hello, learner. Keep both single quotes. Compile and find the changed string in parameters.greeting.defaultValue.
bicep-first-words.expected: The JSON contains parameters.greeting.defaultValue = Hello, learner, and outputs.message refers to greeting. No resource exists.
terms: Declares an input: a value the file accepts.
Names information ARM can return after a deployment.
The value is text; keep quotes around a text literal.

bicep-workspace.title: Make Your Practice Folder
bicep-workspace.code:
param greeting string = 'Hello, CloudSeam'
output message string = greeting
bicep-workspace.task: On your Windows workstation open File Explorer → Documents → create CloudSeam-Bicep. Open that folder in VS Code using File → Open Folder. Create main.bicep and paste the example. In Terminal → New Terminal choose PowerShell and run Get-Location. Save with Ctrl+S.
bicep-workspace.expected: Get-Location ends in Documents\CloudSeam-Bicep. VS Code shows main.bicep, not main.bicep.txt. Browser practice works even before local tools are installed.
terms: The filename. .bicep tells the editor which language to use.
A displayed PowerShell prompt; do not paste PS, the path or > as a command.
Saves the editor buffer to the file the local CLI reads.

bicep-toolchain.title: Install and Check the Tools
bicep-toolchain.code:
param greeting string = 'Hello, CloudSeam'
output message string = greeting
bicep-toolchain.task: Install VS Code, the Microsoft Bicep extension and Azure CLI from the linked official pages. Reopen PowerShell after installation. Run az version, then az bicep install, then az bicep version, then az bicep build --file .\main.bicep. Record the versions. No az login is required for this local file.
bicep-toolchain.expected: main.json appears beside main.bicep. If az is not recognized, reopen the terminal and check the official CLI installation; do not substitute a random installer.
terms: Compiles the file and performs compiler/linter diagnostics.
Selects a file in the current folder.

bicep-errors.title: Fix One Error at a Time
bicep-errors.code:
param greeting string = 'Hello, CloudSeam'
output message string = greeting
bicep-errors.task: In the practice editor remove the closing quote after CloudSeam. Compile. Read the first diagnostic and its line. Restore the quote and compile again. Compare errors with warnings; a warning deserves review even when JSON is emitted.
bicep-errors.expected: The damaged file produces real diagnostics. The repaired file produces ARM JSON. Neither result checks Azure permissions.
terms: A compiler message with a severity and source location.
Prevents a valid template from being emitted.
A concern to review; it may not prevent compilation.

bicep-inputs.title: Inputs, Derived Values and Fixed Words
bicep-inputs.code:
@allowed([
  'dev'
  'test'
])
param environment string = 'dev'
var resourceName = 'app-${environment}'
output plannedName string = resourceName
bicep-inputs.task: Change the environment default from dev to test. Leave the allowed choices and resourceName expression intact. Compile; explain why the expression still appears in JSON rather than a deployed final name.
bicep-inputs.expected: The default is test. The variable expression refers to the parameter. Azure evaluates that expression at deployment time; the browser has not evaluated a live resource.
terms: An input you can provide separately for each deployment.
A derived value: its result changes when environment changes.
Language keywords stay spelled exactly this way; your identifiers and allowed input values can differ.

bicep-types.title: Text, Numbers, Lists and Objects
bicep-types.task: Change serverCount to 3, not '3'. Change enableFeature to true, without quotes. Add a third team to the array. Compile and inspect each parameter type in JSON.
bicep-types.expected: int is compiled as int, bool as bool, and the team list remains an array. Quoting 3 where an int is required causes a type diagnostic.

bicep-resource.title: Read Your First Resource
bicep-resource.task: Read the resource declaration from left to right using the numbered picture. Change Standard_LRS to Standard_GRS, compile, and find resources[0].sku.name. Restore Standard_LRS for the remaining class.
bicep-resource.expected: The generated resource type is Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts, its API version is 2023-05-01 and its SKU matches your edit. Creating it later could incur storage charges.
terms: Declares a resource and its Bicep symbolic name.
Provider/type and the API schema version. Use a documented supported version.
Service settings: HTTPS only, minimum TLS and no anonymous blob access in this example.

bicep-json.title: Read the JSON Under the Bicep
bicep-json.task: Compile, then open Generated ARM JSON. Find parameters, resources and outputs. Match the Bicep storage resource to its JSON type, apiVersion, name, sku and properties. Locally open main.json read-only for comparison; keep editing main.bicep.
bicep-json.expected: You can point to the same storage declaration in both formats. Expressions in square-bracket strings are ARM expressions, not literal final deployed values.
terms: JSON requires quoted property names and commas between properties.
Information the deployment can return; never output credentials.

bicep-guards.title: Add Guardrails Before Resources
bicep-guards.task: Change serverCount default to 0 and compile; read the constraint diagnostic. Restore 2. Find secureString for adminPassword in JSON. Never type a real password into browser practice, source control or a parameter file.
bicep-guards.expected: The bad default is flagged. The secret input is secureString in JSON. Secure typing does not make a hard-coded secret safe.
terms: Restricts a parameter to named choices.
Suppresses normal parameter-value logging/display in ARM; still obtain secrets through an approved secret workflow.

bicep-dependencies.title: Understand What Depends on What
bicep-dependencies.task: Find networkSecurityGroup: { id: nsg.id }. Compile and locate the generated dependency. Explain why the NSG must be available before the dependent VNet configuration. Do not add dependsOn just to repeat a dependency already expressed by a reference.
bicep-dependencies.expected: The VNet template contains a dependency on the NSG. ARM can schedule independent resources in parallel; it is not simply reading top to bottom.
terms: A symbolic reference that expresses an implicit dependency.
An explicit resource dependency when a real ordering relationship cannot be expressed naturally.
References an already present resource; it does not create that resource or check its live existence during local compilation.

bicep-network.title: Build a VNet, Subnet and NSG
bicep-network.task: Find 10.42.0.0/16 and its apps subnet 10.42.1.0/24. They are private example ranges, not discovered lab addresses. Read the deny rule’s direction, access, priority and ports. Compile and count the two top-level resources.
bicep-network.expected: The template contains one NSG and one VNet with an embedded subnet. The explicit priority-4096 deny blocks inbound including traffic normally allowed by default NSG inbound rules; no public IP or admin port is opened.
terms: Who sends the traffic and where it goes.
Lower numbers are evaluated before higher numbers for matching NSG rules.
Network packet rules versus identity membership; do not interchange their resource types.

bicep-existing.title: Reference an Existing Resource
bicep-existing.task: Compile and inspect resources: the existing NSG is not a new resource declaration. Change existingNsgName and observe the parameter default. Do not interpret successful compilation as proof that either NSG exists in your subscription.
bicep-existing.expected: The template describes a reference/output without creating an NSG. Azure access and existence require an authorized live check later.
terms: Use a resource already managed elsewhere.
The subscription/resource group where a name is resolved; this example uses the current resource-group scope.
A resource identifier expression; constructing it locally does not contact Azure.

bicep-loops.title: Plan Multiple Servers with a Loop
bicep-loops.task: Find the NIC loop and VM loop. Change serverCount default from 2 to 3, then compile. Follow nics[i].id to see which NIC each VM uses. Read the JSON copy blocks: they express repetition; two declaration blocks do not mean only two deployed instances.
bicep-loops.expected: The parameter default is 3 and both copy counts refer to serverCount. Each VM references its matching NIC. No VM is created in browser practice.
terms: Repeat for indices 0 through serverCount minus 1.
Use the NIC at this VM’s index.
A training limit, not a guarantee that three VMs are affordable or available.

bicep-server-settings.title: Read the VM Settings Before You Build
bicep-server-settings.task: Locate imageReference, vmSize, osDisk, identity and disablePasswordAuthentication. Explain each before changing it. Keep the example size but check its availability and quota before live validation. Never paste an SSH private key; sshPublicKey expects only a public key during a real deployment.
bicep-server-settings.expected: The template has no public-IP resource, disables password authentication and assigns a system-managed identity. No access roles are granted by assigning an identity. The explicit inbound deny means management/application traffic is not yet allowed.
terms: Azure manages this VM identity’s lifecycle; RBAC permissions require separate approved assignments.
Publisher, offer, SKU and version identify the OS image; verify availability in the chosen region.
The OS disk remains a billable resource after deployment; stopping a VM does not remove disks.

bicep-software.title: Install Software with Cloud-Init

files.cloud-init.yml:
#cloud-config
package_update: true
packages:
  - nginx
runcmd:
  - [systemctl, enable, --now, nginx]

bicep-software.task: Open the cloud-init.yml companion file in the practice panel. Match packages: nginx with the systemctl enable command. Compile main.bicep with the companion file included. The NSG still denies inbound; installing a web server does not make it reachable.
bicep-software.expected: The ARM VM osProfile contains Base64-encoded customData. Compilation proves the file can be read and embedded, not that apt reached a mirror or NGINX started inside a real guest.
terms: Reads a local companion file at compile time.
Encoding for customData, not encryption. Never include secrets.
OS first-boot configuration versus an Azure extension resource; choose a supported mechanism and make retries safe.

bicep-modules.title: Split a Network into a Module
bicep-modules.task: Open network.bicep in the companion-file panel. Find its prefix input and subnetId output. In main.bicep change environment to test; compile both files. Inspect the nested deployment and output reference in JSON.
bicep-modules.expected: The module is embedded as a nested deployment template. network.outputs.subnetId connects parent and child. A missing file or misspelled parameter produces diagnostics.
terms: Values the parent passes to the child’s declared parameters.
The module’s declared output, not a free-form field name.

bicep-environments.title: Separate Dev and Test Inputs
bicep-environments.code:
@allowed([
  'dev'
  'test'
])
param environment string = 'dev'
var resourceName = 'app-${environment}'
output plannedName string = resourceName
bicep-environments.task: Download the example main.bicep and dev.bicepparam. Save both in your CloudSeam-Bicep folder. Open dev.bicepparam in VS Code: using './main.bicep' selects the blueprint; param environment = 'dev' selects the value. Run az bicep build-params --file .\dev.bicepparam locally. Duplicate as test.bicepparam and change only dev to test.
bicep-environments.expected: The local CLI emits a parameters JSON file. The browser practice compiles main.bicep only; it does not validate .bicepparam files. The defaults and environment-specific overrides have separate jobs.
terms: Selects the blueprint for a .bicepparam file.
Used when an input is not overridden; not a permanent constant.
Names, counts and approved regions may differ; keywords and the module contract stay stable.

bicep-azure-checks.title: Validate Against Azure and Preview Changes
bicep-azure-checks.task: First compile locally. In your own Azure CLI session run az login using Microsoft’s local sign-in flow; never enter credentials on this class page. Run az account show and confirm the approved subscription. Use an existing empty training resource group approved by your organization. Run the validation commands below with its name. Stop if access, policy, quota or region errors appear.
bicep-azure-checks.expected: A successful validate response is recorded separately from a what-if result. Read Create/Modify/Delete/NoChange and unresolved expressions. Do not proceed on unexpected deletes, replacements or scope changes. The class never runs Azure operations for you.
terms: Ask ARM to validate this template at the selected scope; provider checks depend on permissions and CLI version.
Preview proposed changes; unresolved expressions and provider behavior can limit accuracy.
An actual deployment command, deliberately separate from this practice checker.

bicep-capstone.title: Write Your Own Private Server Plan
bicep-capstone.task: Choose Start blank in the practice editor. Write parameters for location, prefix, serverCount (1–3), adminUsername and secure sshPublicKey. Declare an NSG, VNet/apps subnet, NIC loop and Linux VM loop. Use private NICs, SSH-key authentication and managed OS disks. No public IP, inbound allow rule or hard-coded secret. Compile in small chunks. Use Show example only after trying.
bicep-capstone.expected: Your code compiles and its JSON contains the correct resource types and loop counts. Manually check the five requirements in the panel; compilation alone does not grade network safety or enterprise readiness. Save the script and your explanation in the notebook.
terms: A parameter you choose, such as serverCount.
An expression built from inputs, such as a resource name.
A relationship such as a VM needing its NIC; different from the input/derived-value distinction.

bicep-handoff.title: Review, Deploy Deliberately and Clean Up
bicep-handoff.task: Create a pull-request-style note: purpose; changed inputs; compiler version; generated resource types; validation/what-if evidence; estimate; approved subscription/group; verification owner; rollback plan. Real deployment is optional and requires your own budget and approval. After an approved deployment verify NICs, NSG association, VM provisioning and guest software separately.
bicep-handoff.expected: Your notebook distinguishes compiled, Azure-validated, previewed, deployed and runtime-verified evidence. For a disposable lab, list resources before approved resource-group deletion; never delete a shared or production group. Reverting source does not automatically reverse a deployment.
terms: Repeatedly requesting the same state should not create duplicate named resources; guest scripts must also be safe to retry.
Manages declared resources without treating omitted declarations as automatic deletion requests.
Review the exact disposable scope and costs; snapshots, disks and other retained items may continue billing.
